newsitem.title: GERMANY: KAL drops ex-mainland Europe rate rise.
newsitem.headline: KAL drops ex-mainland Europe rate rise.

text.p: Korean Air Lines (KAL) said it has dropped plans for a five to 10 per cent ex-mainland Europe air cargo rates rise this autumn due to market competition.
But it will no longer offer cheap ad-hoc rates to fill surplus capacity in a yield-protecting move.
On September 3, KAL said it expected European stations in Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Basle and Brussels to agree to an across the board rise of five to 10 per cent from October or November.
But Robert Instinsky, KAL cargo sales manager Germany, told Reuters that the airline's European managers over-ruled head office proposals for higher rates at a Frankfurt meeting last week.
"The European (managers') group decided not to go ahead (with the rise)," he said.
KAL could not afford to raise rates after the Deutsche Lufthansa AG decision to keep Germany to Korea rates stable, he pointed out.
"Our general selling tariff for KAL in Germany remains the same, neither up nor down," he said.
KAL Europe sales managers also decided only to offer ad-hoc rates for large shipments and not to go below "the pain barrier" by filling capacity at any price, he said.
"On ad-hoc rates we will not be so cheap as before since we have adjusted our rates with the general trend," he added.
Korean Air last adjusted official ex-Europe rates in April 1996. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
